# ai-jury — full reference

> Install once. Run a cross-vendor review jury anywhere.

A small, stdlib-only Python CLI that orchestrates native coding-agent CLIs from
different vendors to review the same diff/PR, debate, verify, and synthesize one
verdict. This file is a fuller agent-readable reference; it links to canonical docs
rather than duplicating them.

## What it is / is not

- **Is:** a local-first orchestrator that drives each vendor's native agent CLI
  (`claude`, `codex`, `agy`) as headless subprocesses — plus an optional local /
  open-weight reviewer over an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint — through an adversarial
  review + debate + verification pipeline, and renders one report (markdown/JSON/SARIF).
- **Is not:** a hosted review SaaS, a dashboard product, a general multi-agent
  framework, or an auto-apply patch tool. It can emit *inspectable* suggested patches for
  verified findings (`--suggest-patches`) but never applies them. Scope stays on review
  orchestration.

## Install & requirements

- Python ≥3.11. Zero runtime dependencies (stdlib: `subprocess`, `tomllib`,
  `concurrent.futures`, `argparse`).
- `pipx install ai-jury` → `jury` entry point (once published; until then
  `pipx install git+https://github.com/berkayturanci/ai-jury.git`).
  `pip install -e .` for dev. Run `jury init` to scaffold a `jury.toml`.
- Install at least one agent CLI: `claude` (Claude Code), `codex` (OpenAI Codex CLI),
  `agy` (Google Antigravity); OR run a free **local / open-weight** model via Ollama (or
  any OpenAI-compatible server) as a `vendor = "local"` agent. Missing/unreachable agents
  are skipped unless `--strict`.
- `gh` (GitHub CLI) is required for `--pr` input and `--post-summary`/`--post-inline`.
- Supported platforms: see [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md#supported-platforms)
  (Linux primary; macOS/Windows tested on the latest Python; live CLIs depend on each
  vendor's own OS support).

## Pipeline

1. **Round 1 — independent review.** Each available agent reviews the diff with the same
   rubric (correctness → security → regressions → tests), concurrently.
2. **Round 2 — cross-examination (optional, `rounds = 2`).** Each agent sees the diff,
   its own review, and the others' reviews; emits AGREE / DISPUTE / MISSED. Needs ≥2 agents.
   With `early_stop = true` this is adaptive: unanimous panels skip it; disagreement runs
   up to `max_rounds`.
3. **Verification pass (optional, `verify = true`).** The chair re-judges each finding
   (verified / unsupported / needs-human-decision) to drop false positives before synthesis.
4. **Synthesis.** The `chair` agent consolidates into one verdict (APPROVE / COMMENT /
   REQUEST CHANGES) with consensus, disputed, and single-reviewer findings.

Cross-cutting: secrets are redacted and the diff scanned for injection before send; large
diffs are filtered (binary/generated/path globs) and **chunked**; the run is bounded by an
optional **budget** (`total_timeout`/`phase_timeout`) with opt-in **retries**; results can
be served from / stored in an optional **cache** (`--cache`). Full detail:
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Subcommands

- `jury init [--agents a,b,c] [--rounds N] [-o jury.toml] [--force]` — scaffold a
  config; detects installed agents + local models. `--list-agents`, `--list-models`.
  `--preset offline|fast|balanced|thorough` for one-command setup.
- `jury config show` — print the effective resolved config and its source;
  `jury config path` — print the resolved config path.
- `jury cache clear` (alias `--clear-cache`) — delete the local result cache.
- `jury comment --text "/jury review …" --pr N` — parse an allowlisted PR-comment
  command (`review`/`summary`, `--rounds` only) and dispatch a safe run (`--print-args`
  to just resolve, `--no-post` to skip posting).

## CLI flags

Input (choose one): `--pr <num/url>` (+ optional `--repo owner/name`), `--diff-file <path|->`.

- `--config <path>` — path to `jury.toml`; `--config-validate` validates and exits;
  `--strict-config` treats config warnings as errors.
- `--policy <path>` — optional repository review policy (else auto-discovers
  `.jury/policy.toml`).
- `--rounds <n>` — fixed rounds (1=review, 2=+debate); disables early-stop.
- `--early-stop` / `--no-early-stop`, `--max-rounds <n>` — adaptive debate (issue #40).
- `--chair <name>` — agent that synthesizes. `--seed <n>` — reproducible orchestration.
- `--verify` / `--no-verify` — verification round (default from config).
- `--total-timeout <s>`, `--phase-timeout <s>`, `--retries <n>` — run budget + retries (#30).
- `--max-diff-bytes <n>`, `--chunk` / `--no-chunk`, `--exclude <glob>`, `--include <glob>`
  — large-diff filtering/chunking (#31).
- `--auto` — auto-depth: set rounds/verify from a pre-review diff profile (#120; config `auto_depth`).
- `--incremental` — review only changes since the last jury run on `--pr` (#9).
- `--suggest-patches`, `--patches-out <path>` — inspectable patches for verified findings (#10).
- `--cache`, `--cache-dir <path>`, `--clear-cache` — optional result cache (#33).
- `--context-mode diff-only|expanded`, `--redact` / `--no-redact` — what leaves your machine.
- `--format markdown|json|sarif`, `-o/--output <path>`, `--metadata-json <path>`.
- `--post-summary` (alias `--post`), `--post-inline`, `--dry-run`, `--label` — GitHub output.
- `--post-progress` — live sticky PR status comment updated each round/chunk (#125; needs `--pr`).
- `--post-mode single|phased` — `phased` posts Round 1 / debate / decision as separate comments (#126).
- `--ci`, `--fail-on <sev,...>` — CI gating.
- `--mock`, `--strict`, `--doctor`, `-q/--quiet`, `--version`.

## Configuration schema — `jury.toml`

```toml
[jury]
rounds = 2          # 1 = review only, 2 = review + debate
chair  = "claude"   # which agent synthesizes the verdict
timeout = 300       # per-agent wall-clock seconds (hung CLI killed at this bound)
parallel = true
verify = true
# early_stop = false ; max_rounds = 3            # adaptive rounds (#40)
# auto_depth = false                              # risk-aware auto-depth (#120; CLI --auto)
# total_timeout = 1200 ; phase_timeout = 600 ; retries = 0   # run budget (#30)

[jury.ci]
fail_on = ["critical", "major"]   # severities that fail `--ci`
ignore_unverified = true

[jury.context]
mode = "diff-only"      # "diff-only" (default) or "expanded"
redact_secrets = true   # scrub recognized secrets before sending (default on)

[jury.diff]           # large-diff handling (#31), all optional
# max_bytes = 200000 ; chunk = false ; exclude_generated = true
# exclude = ["docs/**"] ; include = []

[[agent]]
name = "claude"
vendor = "anthropic"    # anthropic | openai | google | local
command = "claude"
# model = "claude-opus-4-8"
extra_args = ["--output-format", "text", "--disallowed-tools", "Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,Bash", "--dangerously-skip-permissions"]

# A free, offline local / open-weight reviewer (#43):
# [[agent]]
# name = "qwen"
# vendor = "local"
# model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
# endpoint = "http://localhost:11434/v1"   # OpenAI-compatible (Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM/LM Studio)
```

Scaffold the file with `jury init` instead of writing it by hand. See
[docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) for every field.

## Adapter contract

Each adapter (in `src/ai_jury/adapters.py`) knows only how to reach one
agent; the orchestrator owns prompt content. Adding a vendor is a ~20-line addition.
Adapters fail soft — a missing CLI, **non-zero exit (even with stdout)**, timeout, or an
unreachable local endpoint (`connection_error`) becomes a non-fatal
`AgentResult(ok=False, error=…)`; the run continues unless `--strict`.

**Secure by default:** reviewers read attacker-controlled diffs, so they run sandboxed —
Claude `--disallowed-tools Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,Bash`, Codex `-s read-only`,
Antigravity `--sandbox`; `privilege.py` audits this. Invocations:

- Anthropic `ClaudeAdapter`: `claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format text`
- OpenAI `CodexAdapter`: `codex exec` (prompt on stdin), `-s read-only`
- Google `AgyAdapter`: `agy --print "<prompt>" --sandbox`
- local `LocalAdapter`: HTTP `POST {endpoint}/v1/chat/completions` (stdlib `urllib`)
- `MockAdapter`: deterministic, phase-aware output; no subprocess (tests/CI).

## Output formats

- Report to stdout or `-o <file>` in `--format markdown` (default), `json`, or `sarif`.
  Samples: mock [docs/example-run.md](docs/example-run.md); a real 4-vendor run
  [docs/example-live-review.md](docs/example-live-review.md).
- Structured findings keyed by `{severity, file, line, claim}` feed consensus tiers; a
  deterministic PR-level classification + run metadata (`--metadata-json`) are emitted too.
- GitHub: one summary comment (`--post-summary`) and/or inline review comments
  (`--post-inline`) via `gh`; opt-in classification labels (`--label`).
- Suggested patches for verified findings (`--suggest-patches`, `--patches-out`).
- CI: exit code is non-zero when blocking findings remain (`--ci`, `--fail-on`).

## Security / data-flow model

- **Context modes:** `diff-only` (default) sends only the diff; `expanded` adds PR
  title/body. No source files outside the diff, no repo history, no env vars are read or sent.
- **Secret redaction (on by default):** the diff and context pass through
  `redaction.py`, masking PEM keys, AWS keys, GitHub/OpenAI tokens, `Bearer` tokens, and
  generic `api_key`/`secret`/`token` assignments → `[REDACTED:<kind>]`.
- **Posting** sends the rendered report/comments to the GitHub API; `--dry-run` previews
  the inline payload with no network call.
- Repository security posture: CodeQL + OpenSSF Scorecard + SHA-pinned Actions.
- Canonical reference: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Skill / distribution

A Claude Code skill ships in [skill/ai-jury/](skill/ai-jury/SKILL.md);
drop it into a project's `.claude/skills/` to convene the jury on demand. The repo is
also installable as a single-plugin marketplace via `.claude-plugin/` manifests, and a
platform support matrix lives in [docs/platforms.md](docs/platforms.md).

## Status

The v0.2–v0.6 roadmap has landed: structured findings + tiered consensus, verification,
anonymized rebuttal, adaptive early-stop, CI gating, secure-by-default sandboxing, run
budget/retries, large-diff chunking, result cache, incremental review, suggested patches,
comment-command triggering, a local/open-weight adapter, and `jury init`. Phased
history in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md); open items under
[milestones](https://github.com/berkayturanci/ai-jury/milestones).

## Troubleshooting

- **An agent is skipped:** its CLI isn't installed/on PATH. Install it or run `--mock`.
  Use `--strict` to fail instead of skipping.
- **Hang:** a CLI exceeding `timeout` is killed and recorded as a failed agent.
- **`--pr` errors:** ensure `gh` is installed and authenticated for the repo.
- **No debate:** debate needs ≥2 agents whose round-1 call succeeded; otherwise it falls
  back to review + synthesis.
- **Codex structured output ignored:** disable MCP servers for review runs (see
  [docs/feasibility.md](docs/feasibility.md)).
